newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW-China plays to add colour to HK handover.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-China plays to add colour to HK handover.

text.p: July listings of China-related shares are expected to add colour to celebrations surrounding Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule and could give the counters an initial boost in the market, analysts said.

Seven or eight companies, most of them China plays, are planning to list shares on the Hong Kong stock exchange around the handover at midnight on June 30 and hope to use the timing to best advantage, market sources said.
"It makes sense for these companies to list in July due to the expected strong market sentiment and also when the world is focusing on Hong Kong," said one analyst.

Among the companies expected to list around the handover are Jingtai Co, the investment arm of the Beijing municipal government, and Tianjin Industrial Holdings Ltd, backed by the Tianjin municipal government, market sources said.

The stock market is expected to be buoyant around the change of sovereignty as investors anticipate further economic integration of Hong Kong and China, DBS Securities director of research Percy Au-young said.
Companies would be able to issue shares at a higher price-earnings multiple at that time, he said.
"It will add some colour to the Hong Kong handover," he added.
Analysts said Chinese authorities want to maintain a picture of stability and prosperity around the handover period and would be choosy about the red chips and H-shares they allow to list.
Red chips are Hong Kong companies with strong China ties, while H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in China-incorporated companies.

"Chinese authorities are likely to give the green light only to strong quality new listings and particularly so for those trying to list in July," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at Impac Asset Management.
Some companies may even wish to delay their initial public offerings (IPO) since investors may be distracted around that time by the handover celebrations, analysts said.
"Foreign investors will tend to adopt a wait-and-see attitude to see how things go before they invest or re-rate their weighting here in Hong Kong," Tang said.
The IPO schedule for the second half of the year looks tightly packed with more than 50 candidates lining up for Hong Kong listings, corporate finance sources said.
Red chips, H-shares and other China plays are likely to dominate the new issue market, they added.
